instantiated_cells.justification: A "legislative agent" is any individual engaged (employed or retained for compensation) to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes — no dollar threshold; any compensation triggers registration.
The definition of legislative agent is based on being engaged for compensation to actively advocate; the statute does not define a lobbyist by the amount of expenditures the lobbyist makes.

The lobbyist definition uses the qualitative phrase "during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes" with no quantified time threshold.

Meals and food/beverage expenditures need only be itemized once they cumulatively exceed $50 per calendar year per particular official, establishing a $50 de minimis itemization threshold for that expenditure category.

The registration and expenditure-statement filing duties under §§101.72 and 101.73 apply to all engaged legislative agents and employers without any overall dollar-amount de minimis exemption from filing.

Neither the definition of legislative agent nor the registration/filing requirements include a percentage-of-time threshold that exempts a lobbyist from filing disclosure; the standard is the qualitative "one of the individual's main purposes."

content.text:
I'll analyze each question against the Ohio statute text.

**Row 001 - Compensation threshold for lobbyist registration:** §101.70(F) defines "legislative agent" as anyone "engaged during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes." §101.70(H) defines "engage" as employed/retained "for compensation." No dollar threshold — any compensation triggers it.

**Row 002 - Lobbyist expenditure threshold:** No expenditure-based definition of lobbyist exists; the definition is compensation-based.

**Row 003 - Time threshold:** §101.70(F) requires actively advocating "as one of the individual's main purposes" — qualitative, not a specific time quantity.

**Row 004 - Itemization threshold:** §101.73(B)(3) sets a $50 cumulative threshold for meals/food/beverages per calendar year per official before itemization is required.

**Row 005 - Filing exemption de minimis:** No overall dollar exemption from filing exists.

**Row 006 - Time-percent filing exemption:** No percentage-of-time exemption exists in the statute.
